where: Section 1, last line of the PFD section
problem: The claim that 'One PFD replaces three mechanical dials' undercounts badly and contradicts the chapter's own list. A PFD carries attitude, airspeed, altitude, vertical speed and heading, so it replaces at least five instruments from the old panel (attitude indicator, airspeed indicator, altimeter, vertical speed indicator, heading indicator/HSI), more on a full six-pack.
fix: One PFD replaces five or more mechanical instruments — attitude indicator, airspeed indicator, altimeter, vertical speed indicator and heading indicator — and saves panel area.

problem: Naming white as the colour of advisory messages is not standard. On Boeing EICAS the advisory level is normally shown in cyan/blue and white is used for memo/status lines; on Airbus ECAM, status/memo text is white. A student who writes 'advisory = white' in an exam can lose marks.
fix: Alert levels rise from advisory (typically cyan/blue) to caution (amber) to warning (red); a warning usually brings an aural alert too. White is used for memo or status text, not for the advisory level.

problem: 'Electronic system monitor displays' is not a standard textbook term; presenting it as a syllabus label may confuse students who meet only EICAS and ECAM in their notes.
fix: Drop the invented label, or write: EICAS and ECAM are both engine-indication and crew-alerting displays; some notes call them engine and system monitors.
